claim: When a tool fetches addresses that strangers control (agent manifests, peer networks, receipts), route every read through one guarded fetch that resolves once and connects to the checked address, refuses private ranges on every redirect hop, caps the body at a ceiling derived from a measured real document, and times out absolutely, because a second DNS lookup or an unchecked redirect turns a checker into an SSRF probe.
because: plumbline src/net/safe-fetch.ts landed with 20 tests (hostname resolving to a private range, redirect hop to 169.254.169.254, v4-mapped v6); the registry map scored this context weakly governed: the rule exists only as a paragraph inside origin-signed-record-with-index-as-cache.
